title: [CmdPal] Some apps which self-elevate do not run when launched from Command Palette
summary: A contributor reproduced the self-elevating app launch failure and isolated it to ShellExecute running on a thread without an active message pump.

judgment.rationale: The new reproduction video, error text, and controlled thread experiments materially narrow the failure. Both normal and elevated launch paths wrap ShellExecute in Task.Run; a dedicated STA thread only succeeds when it also runs a Win32 message pump.
evidence: HWiNFO64 launches from Windows Search but not from Command Palette after the UAC prompt.
The logged failure is ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED for the shortcut path.
The failure reproduces with both the shortcut and resolved executable.
AppCommand.StartExe and RunAsAdminCommand both call Process.Start from Task.Run.
The contributor reports success on a dedicated STA thread with an active Win32 message pump.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design that centralizes shell launch on a reusable STA message-loop dispatcher and validates both normal and elevated app launch.

fix_assessment.rationale: The contributor has a strong investigation but no linked pull request or concrete fix is present yet.

proposed_fixes.title: Dispatch ShellExecute launches through a reusable STA message loop
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Command Palette invokes UseShellExecute-based normal and elevated launches inside Task.Run. The resulting worker thread lacks the shell-compatible apartment and message-pump context required by some self-elevating applications.
plan: Introduce a shared CmdPal Apps shell-launch dispatcher backed by one long-lived STA thread with an active Win32 message loop.
Route AppCommand.StartExe and RunAsAdminCommand through the dispatcher instead of creating arbitrary ThreadPool work.
Propagate launch failures through existing logging without blocking the UI thread.
Add focused dispatcher tests and verify normal, elevated, shortcut, and resolved-executable launches.
verification: Launch HWiNFO64 and LenovoLegionToolkit normally and elevated from Command Palette.
Confirm the UAC flow completes and the application window appears.
Verify ordinary non-elevated app launches and packaged-app activation remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The thread experiments strongly support the message-pump hypothesis, but the shared dispatcher lifetime and shutdown behavior still require implementation validation.

issue_context.summary: UseShellExecute succeeds from Windows Search but fails from Command Palette for some self-elevating applications after UAC approval.
known_information: The issue affects HWiNFO64 and LenovoLegionToolkit.
A reproduction video and exact ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED log were supplied.
Both shortcut and resolved executable paths fail.
Both normal and Run as administrator Command Palette paths use Task.Run around Process.Start.
A dedicated STA thread with an active message pump succeeds in the contributor's experiment.
inferences: The shell launch requires a message-pumping apartment for this elevation path.
A shared dispatcher is safer than creating a new thread and pump for every invocation.
issue_context.analysis: The new evidence replaces the prior generic diagnostic request with a concrete implementation boundary. The design must preserve the existing protection against WinUI reentrancy while supplying the shell context that Task.Run lacks.
initial_investigation: Read the new reproduction and investigation comment.
Verified AppCommand.StartExe and RunAsAdminCommand both execute Process.Start from Task.Run in the current source.
Confirmed packaged-app activation uses a separate activation manager path.

actions.label: Design STA shell-launch dispatcher
actions.note: Approval starts fork-side design work only; no upstream write occurs automatically.

reproduce.version: Current main and PowerToys 0.100.2 for comparison
prerequisites: Ensure the application self-elevates and is indexed by Command Palette
steps: Launch the application normally from Command Palette and approve UAC.
Launch the same shortcut from Windows Search as a control.
Capture the Command Palette log and whether an application window appears.
reproduce.expected_result: The application opens after UAC approval from both Command Palette launch paths.
reproduce.actual_result_reported: UAC appears, then Command Palette logs ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED and no application window opens.

upstream_safety.detail: No public mutation was made to microsoft/PowerToys.
